arxiv-2410-07970.title: Mapping Hong Kong’s Financial Ecosystem: A Network Analysis of the SFC’s Licensed Professionals and Institutions
arxiv-2410-07970.creator: Abdulla AlKetbi 1,2,3, Gautier Marti 3, Khaled AlNuaimi 1,3, Raed Jaradat 1, Andreas Henschel 1
arxiv-2410-07970.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Abdulla AlKetbi 1,2,3, Gautier Marti 3, Khaled AlNuaimi 1,3, Raed Jaradat 1, Andreas Henschel 1. We present the first study of the Public Register of Licensed Persons and Registered Institutions maintained by the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) through the lens of complex network analysis. This dataset, spanning 21 years with daily granularity, provides a unique view of the evolving social network between licensed professionals and their affiliated firms in Hong Kong’s financial sector.

arxiv-2501-00107.title: An Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Electricity Consumption Using Reinforcement Learning and Time Series Forest Based Framework
arxiv-2501-00107.creator: Jihan Ghanim, Mariette Awad
arxiv-2501-00107.description: Abstract Anomaly detection (AD) plays a crucial role in time series applications, primarily because time series data is employed across real-world scenarios. Detecting anomalies poses significant challenges since anomalies take diverse forms making them hard to pinpoint accurately. Previous research has explored different AD models, making specific assumptions with varying sensitivity toward particular anomaly types.

arxiv-2501-17132.title: ASTRAL : Automated Safety Testing of Large Language Models
arxiv-2501-17132.creator: Miriam Ugarte, Pablo Valle, Jose Antonio Parejo, Sergio Segura, Aitor Arrieta
arxiv-2501-17132.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently gained significant attention due to their ability to understand and generate sophisticated human-like content. However, ensuring their safety is paramount as they might provide harmful and unsafe responses. Existing LLM testing frameworks address various safety-related concerns (e.g., drugs, terrorism, animal abuse) but often face challenges due to unbalanced and obsolete datasets.

arxiv-2512-13608.title: DBT-DINO: Towards Foundation model based analysis of Digital Breast Tomosynthesis
arxiv-2512-13608.creator: Felix J. Dorfner *, Manon A. Dorster, Ryan Connolly, Oscar Gentilhomme, Edward Gibbs, Steven Graham, Seth Wander, Thomas Schultz, Manisha Bahl, Dania Daye, Albert E. Kim ‡ \ddagger, Christopher P. Bridge ‡ \ddagger
arxiv-2512-13608.description: Abstract Background: Foundation models have shown promise in medical imaging but remain underexplored for three-dimensional imaging modalities. No foundation model currently exists for Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT), despite its use for breast cancer screening. Purpose: To develop and evaluate a foundation model for DBT (DBT-DINO) across multiple clinical tasks and assess the impact of domain-specific pre-training.

pmc-10671329.creator: Marialuisa Menegatto, Adriano Zamperini
pmc-10671329.description: Residents of an extensive area of the Veneto Region (Italy) face one of the largest technological disasters due to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). On the basis of a risk gradient of contamination, the affected territories were divided into 4 areas: Red (of maximum exposure, where a human biomonitoring programme (HBM) was activated), Orange, Yellow, and Green.

pmc-11615344.title: Distribution of C30 carotenoid biosynthesis genes suggests habitat adaptation function in insect-adapted and nomadic Lactobacillaceae
pmc-11615344.creator: Tom Eilers, Marie Legein, Jari Temmermans, Jelle Dillen, Ine Vandendriessche, Koen Sandra, Peter A. Bron, Stijn Wittouck, Sarah Lebeer
pmc-11615344.description: Carotenoids are membrane-bound pigments that are essential for photosynthesizing plants and algae, widely applied in food, feed and cosmetics due to their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The production of carotenoids, particularly C30 forms, has been documented in some non-photosynthetic prokaryotes. However, their function, distribution and ecology beyond photosynthesizing organisms remains understudied.

pmc-11675089.title: Testing the Isotropic Cauchy Hypothesis
pmc-11675089.creator: Jihad Fahs, Ibrahim Abou-Faycal, Ibrahim Issa
pmc-11675089.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The isotropic Cauchy distribution is a member of the central α-stable family that plays a role in the set of heavy-tailed distributions similar to that of the Gaussian density among finite second-moment laws. Given a sequence of n observations, we are interested in characterizing the performance of Likelihood Ratio Tests, where two hypotheses are plausible for the observed quantities: either isotropic Cauchy or isotropic Gaussian.

pmc-11705449.title: Comments on “Comparative Study on the Efficacy of PRP Gel and UC‐MSCs Gel as Adjuvant Therapies in the Treatment of DFU Wounds”
pmc-11705449.creator: Mostafa Javanian, Mohammad Barary, Majid Khalilizad, Soheil Ebrahimpour
pmc-11705449.description: asma (PRP) gel compares with umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (UC‐MSCs) gel in managing diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs). The authors demonstrated that UC‐MSCs gel was significantly more effective than PRP gel, resulting in quicker wound closure, improved wound healing rates, enhanced control of pain and infection, and better vascular and neurological outcomes.

pmc-12849252.title: Visit‑to‑visit variability of inflammation–immunity indices and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-12849252.creator: Qiajun Du, Youli Zhao, Jing Yang, Yongxin Yang
pmc-12849252.description: BackgroundInflammatory–immune blood indices such as the systemic immune‑inflammation index (SII) relate to outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Visit‑to‑visit variability (VVV) may capture instability of host inflammatory homeostasis that is not reflected by average levels. We examined whether early VVV of these indices predicts overall survival (OS) and adds discriminatory value beyond standard prognostic factors and mean levels.
